items.title: Joey Morant interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, April 2, 2013
items.q: Now we have some watermelon — like George Gershwin said, Get your watermelon today.

ctx.x: Jazz. Because I improvise R&B and gospel. When I improvise jazz I’m thinking how fortunate it would be if the young people, especially the minority — I want to underscore that because they came up from the bottom line — the blacks, the Hispanics, some Jews — if only it would reflect on their structure, life structure, in music, when they start to improvise. Tell a story emphatically about what makes them unique as a person in spite of the conditions, not because of the conditions. So I think of me as being a…

sold watermelon back on the truck in Charleston, South Carolina, I sold apples and oranges. [sings] Get your apples today. And like a typical Little Black Sambo at that time. I say typical because you were expected to act black back then. I call it acting black. Get your watermelon today. Now we have some watermelon — like George Gershwin said, Get your watermelon today. And I sold Christmas trees. I was a hamburger maker, BLT, pig in a blanket which is a hot dog wrapped in cheese. So I did culinary work, I cut…
Well when did the trumpet come along then, to replace those menial jobs?
